subject: Re: Logging & redaction controls — next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Amit Shah <amit.shah@fintechco.com>, Sofia Lopez <sofia.lopez@fintechco.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 25 Jun 2026 14:10:00 -0700
Subject: FintechCo — Logging & redaction follow-up (post-demo)

Thanks again for taking the time today — really appreciate the detailed product questions. Quick recap and the asks we captured on the call so we can align on next steps:

- What you told us: you want access to request/response traces for debugging and audit, but you must ensure PII is not retained in logs longer than 90 days and certain headers must never be persisted.
- Primary redaction concerns you called out: SSNs, full card numbers, CVV, unmasked account numbers, and customer full names in free-text responses.
- Residency: Data must be stored in US-only regions for the PoC.
- Retention: 90 days default, with ability to configure shorter retention per environment.

Next steps from Redwood (proposed):
1) We’ll propose two redaction modes for your review: 
   - Minimal: redact PII from request bodies and headers before any persistent logging; retain hashed trace IDs for correlation.
   - Verbose (debug): allow request/response content to be stored but pass it through a stronger NLP redaction pipeline and tokenization; restricted to a dedicated support-only bucket and access audited.
2) Engineering spec: Rafael to outline a PoC plan for the redaction pipeline (regex + ML entity redactor + heuristics for numeric sequences).
3) Compliance: we’ll attach our SOC2 evidence and a brief on how our retention controls and delete APIs work.

Could you confirm the following so we scope the PoC correctly?
- Do you need response content stored (not just requests) for reproduction of issues?
- Which headers should be treated as sensitive for you (Authorization, Cookie, Set-Cookie, x-session-id, other)?
- Are hashed trace IDs acceptable (one-way hash) or do you require a reversible mapping for support debug?

I’ve attached the redaction_requirements_v2.pdf from our runbook and a sample screenshot of the request log UI. If you prefer, we can schedule a short tech session with Rafael and our infra team next week.

Best,
Marissa

From: Amit Shah <amit.shah@fintechco.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Sofia Lopez <sofia.lopez@fintechco.com>
Date: Thu, 25 Jun 2026 16:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: FintechCo — Logging & redaction follow-up (post-demo)

Thanks Marissa — nice summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Retention: 90 days is our baseline requirement for searchable logs. We may ask for a 30-day window for certain QA environments.
- Response storage: We do need response content for a subset of incidents (fraud investigations). For day-to-day debugging, request-only plus metadata is fine.
- Sensitive headers: please treat Authorization and Set-Cookie as non-persistable. x-b3-traceid and internal trace headers are ok to keep, but we'd prefer them hashed.
- Trace ID mapping: we would prefer a reversible mapping for critical incidents (support-only access) but understand the risk. If reversible, we’ll need strict audit logs and a short TTL (90 days).

Attaching a short doc outlining our redaction matrix and a screenshot of the type of log we export from our systems.

Also: can you confirm that redaction runs prior to any third-party backup or analytics export? That was a key compliance ask.

—Amit
Amit Shah
Head of Platform Security, FintechCo
amit.shah@fintechco.com

Attachments: fintechco_redaction_matrix.pdf (application/pdf), exported-log-example.png (image/png)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Amit Shah <amit.shah@fintechco.com>, Sofia Lopez <sofia.lopez@fintechco.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 26 Jun 2026 08:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: FintechCo — Logging & redaction follow-up (post-demo)

Great questions — thanks for the details. Quick responses and suggested approach so we can agree scope for the PoC: 

- Redaction order: redaction is configurable and can run at the ingestion layer before any backups or downstream exports. We’ll document the pipeline and provide an assurance statement for the PoC.
- Response retention: we can support a hybrid approach — default to request-only retention and provide a gated response-capture mode for tagged incidents. Response captures will be stored in a restricted bucket with strict RBAC and audit trails.
- Headers: we will strip Authorization and Set-Cookie entirely before persistence. For trace headers (x-b3-traceid, x-request-id) we can store a one-way hash by default; for reversible mapping we can implement an encrypted mapping table with audit logs but this will be a scoped feature (adds complexity).
- Redaction tech: proposed pipeline = 1) header-level filters (denylist), 2) regex-based redaction for deterministic patterns (credit card, SSN), 3) ML entity redactor pass for names/email addresses, 4) numeric heuristics to catch token-like sequences. We’ll include a whitelist mechanism for fields you explicitly want preserved.

Next steps we propose: 
- Rafael: produce a 1-page engineering spec (PoC scope, infra changes, estimate) by EOD Tuesday.
- Stephanie: coordinate a 60-minute PoC kickoff with FintechCo for Wed/Thu next week.
- From FintechCo: confirm acceptance of hashed trace IDs vs reversible mapping and provide any additional headers to denylist.

I’m attaching the PoC MAP link here: https://redwood.app/s/FT-4721-MAP and the drive doc with our suggested redaction rules: https://drive.google.com/fintechco/prompt-qa

If that all looks good, we’ll schedule Rafael and one infra engineer to walk through the PoC design.

Thanks,
Marissa

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Fwd: FintechCo — Logging & redaction follow-up (internal)

Internal summary and asks — adding context from the thread above. Keep this tight for eng: 

Summary: FintechCo requires 90-day retention, US-only residency, Authorization/Set-Cookie must be stripped. They are okay with hashed trace IDs by default but have asked for reversible mapping for critical incidents if we can provide audited access and a TTL. They want response captures only for tagged incidents (fraud), not by default.

Action items: 
- Rafael: please produce a 1-page PoC spec that includes:
  * Where the redaction runs (in ingestion cluster vs edge)
  * Proposed stack (regex + spaCy/NER model + heuristics) and fallback rules
  * How we’ll handle reversible trace mapping (encrypted table vs key management) and estimated work effort (dev + ops)
  * Any risk notes for backups/analytics exports and mitigation
- Stephanie: own the customer-facing PoC timeline, confirm Wed/Thu availability for kickoff, and prepare a short compliance packet (SOC2 snapshot, retention controls description).

Let me know if you need me to take any of these on. Rafael — happy to sync 30m after you have a draft.

-Marissa
